steps.name: Verify DE inputs and build ranked gene list
steps.context: Dataset: 12,000 genes x 13 columns Salmon gene-level counts (counts.csv), 12-sample metadata with condition (metadata.csv), and a DESeq2 results table de_results.csv (12,000 rows, 8 columns: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, and remaining statistics columns to be inspected at run time). Condition design: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Known caveat: sample_01 library size ~4x below median. Human skin, atopic dermatitis lesional vs control. User constraint: Python only, no R. The user explicitly wants to start from the existing DE results, so differential expression must not be recomputed.
steps.question: Are counts.csv, metadata.csv, and de_results.csv mutually consistent for the 6 treated vs 6 control contrast, and can a valid HGNC-symbol ranked gene list and significant-gene list be built from the existing DESeq2 statistics without re-running DE?
steps.description: Reads the three input CSVs, checks sample/condition consistency and the sample_01 library-size caveat, resolves gene identifiers to HGNC symbols (mapping Ensembl IDs through the staged UniProt human ID-mapping table if needed), and emits the ranked gene list (Wald statistic, fallback sign(LFC)*-log10(p)) and the padj<0.05 significant-gene list that feed the enrichment steps.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 samples in metadata.csv are present as columns in counts.csv with matching condition labels (6 treated, 6 control); any mismatch is reported, not silently fixed

sample_01's ~4x-below-median library size is quantified in the QC report; its gene-level behavior (e.g., detected-gene count, whether it is an outlier in a simple PCA of variance-stabilized counts) is reported but DE is NOT re-run — the user's DESeq2 table is authoritative

The identifier type of the 'gene' column in de_results.csv is determined (HGNC symbols vs Ensembl IDs); if not HGNC symbols, genes are mapped to HGNC symbols via the staged UniProt human ID-mapping table (offline, /mnt/refs), and the mapping rate and count of unmapped genes are reported

A full ranked list is produced (all 12,000 genes with a statistic): primary ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic column if present, otherwise sign(log2_fold_change) * -log10(p_value); no ties at the top, no NaN statistics, direction convention (positive = up in treated) stated in the output

A significant-gene list for ORA is produced at padj < 0.05 with up/down split counts reported; if fewer than 10 genes are significant the fallback ORA threshold padj < 0.1 is also produced and both are saved
Outputs written as CSV: ranked_gene_list.csv, significant_genes.csv, input_qc_report.md

steps.name: Hallmark GSEA prerank and ORA in Python
steps.context: Inputs from T1S1: ranked_gene_list.csv (gene, statistic, descending) and significant_genes.csv (padj<0.05, with up/down labels). Reference: /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt — 50 HALLMARK_* sets, one per line, tab-separated: set name, URL, member HGNC symbols. Python packages gseapy 1.3.1 and blitzgsea are installed; gseapy.prerank and gseapy.enrich both accept a local GMT path and work fully offline. Note: with 12,000 tested genes the background for ORA must be the DE-tested universe, not all HGNC genes.
steps.question: Which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched among genes up- or down-regulated in treated vs control skin, by both full-rank GSEA and over-representation of significant DE genes?
steps.description: Runs two complementary hallmark enrichment analyses in Python against the local MSigDB Hallmark human GMT: GSEA prerank on the T1S1 ranked list (uses all 12,000 genes, the appropriate test at 6-vs-6) and hypergeometric ORA on the significant genes with the ranked-list universe as background. Reports NES/fold-enrichment with FDR for all 50 sets and flags GSEA-vs-ORA direction conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: Gene sets come from the staged MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1 symbols GMT (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols) resolved offline from the reference store; no Enrichr/API call and no network access anywhere in the script

GSEA prerank (gseapy.prerank) runs on the full ranked list with min_size 15, max_size 500, 1,000 permutations, weighted scoring, seed fixed for reproducibility; every one of the 50 hallmark sets gets a NES, nominal p, and FDR q in the output

ORA (gseapy.enrich or an explicit scipy hypergeometric test) runs on the padj<0.05 significant list against the same GMT with background = all genes in the ranked list (not the whole GMT), BH-corrected

Results report per set: set size after intersecting with the ranked list, NES (GSEA) and fold enrichment (ORA), FDR, and direction (enriched in treated = up, in control = down); sets with conflicting direction between GSEA and ORA are flagged, not averaged
The number of hallmark sets lost to size filtering or zero gene overlap is reported so an empty result is distinguishable from a failed run
Outputs written as CSV: hallmark_gsea_prerank.csv, hallmark_ora.csv

steps.name: Visualize and summarize hallmark enrichment
steps.context: Inputs from T1S2: hallmark_gsea_prerank.csv (per-set NES, p, FDR, leading-edge tags available via gseapy term/gene overlap fields), hallmark_ora.csv (per-set overlap genes, fold enrichment, BH q). The gene x sample counts and per-gene log2_fold_change from de_results.csv are available for the leading-edge heatmap. Python matplotlib, seaborn, adjusttext installed.
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways are confidently enriched in treated vs control skin once GSEA and ORA are cross-read, and which leading-edge genes support each hit?
steps.description: Cross-reads the GSEA and ORA hallmark results, extracts leading-edge genes per enriched set, and produces the final summary: confidence-ranked hallmark hit table, NES/FDR figures, a leading-edge log2FC heatmap, and a markdown summary with explicit 6-vs-6 and sample_01 caveats.
acceptance_criteria: A combined result table ranks hallmark sets by evidence strength: GSEA FDR, ORA FDR, concordant direction, leading-edge/significant gene count; sets significant by both methods with concordant direction are listed as confident calls
Leading-edge genes (GSEA) and significant contributing genes (ORA) are extracted per enriched set and written to a CSV for downstream use

Plots produced as PNG: (1) NES-vs-FDR dot/barplot of all 50 hallmark sets with enriched-direction color coding, (2) ORA -log10(FDR) barplot, (3) heatmap of leading-edge gene log2 fold changes across enriched sets; no network call for any figure

The summary states the up-in-treated and down-in-treated hallmark hits separately, names the supporting leading-edge genes for the top hits, and explicitly caveats that this is a 6-vs-6 design with sample_01's low library size flagged in QC — no mechanistic overclaim
Final deliverables: hallmark_enrichment_summary.md and hallmark_leading_edge_genes.csv alongside the PNG figures

plan.title: Hallmark enrichment in AD treated-vs-control DE
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human skin samples (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) with Salmon gene-level counts and a precomputed DESeq2 results table (12,000 genes) for the treated-vs-control contrast. The user asked specifically which hallmark pathways are enriched, starting from the existing DE results, and requires Python for every script. The plan therefore does not re-run differential expression; it (1) verifies the three inputs are mutually consistent, resolves the DE table's gene identifiers to HGNC symbols, and builds a full ranked gene list plus an ORA gene list from the DE statistics; (2) runs two complementary hallmark enrichment analyses in Python — GSEA prerank on the full ranked list (uses all 12,000 genes, robust at n=12) and over-representation analysis on the significant genes — against the staged MSigDB Hallmark 2026.1 human symbols GMT (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC, no network needed); and (3) visualizes and summarizes concordant hits with leading-edge gene support. Both GSEA and ORA are run because they differ in sensitivity and in what can be called significant with 6-vs-6 samples; concordance between them is the criterion for a confident call.
